title: An SSE comment heartbeat is invisible to page JavaScript
statement: Per the WHATWG specification, a line in an event stream beginning with a colon is ignored by the client parser. A comment heartbeat therefore fires no event and cannot be observed by page code; the specification names its purpose as preventing legacy proxies from dropping an idle connection. Making stream health visible to a client watchdog requires a named event carrying a data field, not a comment.
notes: ⚠️ THIS CORRECTS A PROPOSAL I MADE, and the way it was wrong is worth keeping. QST-0021's measurement showed idle and dead streams are byte-identical, and the fix I offered was a periodic comment frame — which fixes the BYTES and not the VISIBILITY, because the one consumer that needs to see it is the only one specified to ignore it. A transport-level keepalive would have left the page exactly as falsely healthy as before while looking like a solution. ⚠️ Same shape as AST-0022 and AST-0028 once more: a mechanism that appears to close a gap because something is now happening, while the thing that needed to observe it still cannot.
